text:
maria: Quick PSA — FP8 enablement on H100 in the latest canary is showing surprising perf instability. Throughput drops intermittently and KV cache eviction spikes. Posting a short profile and logs so we can triage.

kevin: Thanks, can you paste the perf numbers? latency or throughput regression?

maria: Throughput regression. Microbench on perf harness (batch=8, seq=1024) shows ~18% RPS drop vs int8 baseline and 30-40% variance across runs. Short seq workloads (seq<=64) are worse: jitter +40%. KV metrics show eviction rate jumping during the slow windows.

jon: Is this only on H100 or also L40S?

maria: Mostly H100 in current run, but we reproduced a smaller signal on L40S when transformer-engine fp8 kernels are selected.

tara: Can you share which kernels are being picked? maybe kernel selector is choosing an fp8 path that doesn't play well with the current attention tiling.

maria: Attach from profiler (condensed):

```
Profile summary (canary-2026/03/18):
- model: gpt-like, layers=32
- batch:8 seq:1024 tokens/sec: 12.4k (int8 baseline 15.1k)
- kernel chooser: fp8_attn_v2 -> fp8_gemm_opt -> fp8_output_scale
- percent time in attention kernel: 62%
- avg kernel time variance: 18ms -> spikes to 70ms intermittently
- KV eviction rate: 0.3% -> 5.8% during spike windows
- observed fallback: some layers fallback to int8 mid-run (logs show fallback reasons: "overflow-suspected" then "auto-fallback")
```

kevin: Interesting — fallback mid-run is a red flag. Could be calibration drift or exponent bias saturating with certain sequence lengths. Any calibration data for the fp8 scales?

maria: We used the public calibration pass from last week (calib_v3). The scale histograms show heavier tails for key projections on layers 8-12. I suspect the dynamic range on KV keys is triggering dynamic kernel switches in the transformer engine.

jon: We have two attack vectors: (1) improve the kernel selector heuristic to prefer stable int8 for short seq or high-kv-hit regimes, (2) fix fp8 calibration (wider dynamic range/robust clipping) and add a conservative fallback cooldown to avoid mid-batch churn.

tara: I ran a comboprofile: force kernel=fp8 vs force kernel=int8 for same trace. Forcing int8 eliminates spikes and reduces KV eviction by ~80%. Forcing fp8 yields highest peak throughput but worst variance.

maria: Here's a short snippet of the config I used to reproduce:

```
runtime:
  device: H100
  batch: 8
  seq: 1024
  kernel_selector:
    prefer_fp8: auto
    seq_threshold: 128
  fp8:
    calib_profile: calib_v3
    exponent_bias: auto
    clip_threshold: 6.0
```

kevin: Two quick fixes we can try: lower prefer_fp8 threshold (seq_threshold=256 -> 512) so medium-length requests prefer int8; and add a "fp8-stability-cooldown" that prevents kernel reselect for a short window after fallback.

jon: Agreed. Also add an observability flag to emit "kernel_switch" events with layer id so we can correlate with KV evictions. Right now logs are too coarse.

maria: Filed a mini-epic: FP8-HOTFIX-1887 — add selector heuristics + cooldown + richer kernel_switch telemetry. Will open PR with tests.

tara: For QA: we should add a stress test that runs mixed sequence-length traffic (20/80/300/1024) and validates no mid-run kernel fallback and eviction rate stays below 1%.

ci-bot: build 2891 started for branch fp8-hotfix-1887. Estimated run time ~22m.

kevin: Also think about a lightweight calibration shim that runs per-deploy (1000 sample prompts, compute per-layer scale percentiles) and ships a "deploy-calib" artifact. That could avoid wide-tail surprises in production.

maria: Good idea — we can store calib artifacts keyed by model-version+transformer-engine-config. Redwood console can surface when a deploy uses mismatched calib artifact.

perf-bot: perf alert: canary-h100 FP8 run — p95 latency increased 28% vs baseline at 2026-03-17 15:22:11. Link: https://perf.redwood/alerts/8892

jon: Next steps assigned: maria (kernel switch telemetry + PR), kevin (selector heuristic change + config opt), tara (stress test + QA harness). Let's reconvene after CI run. If CI reproduces we'll rollback fp8 in canary and hold until fixes land. :+1:

maria: Thanks all — I'll post PR link and a short runbook for rollback (force kernel=int8 in runtime) once CI finishes.

kevin: For the runbook: quick command to pin int8: `redwoodctl set-runtime --model my-model --kernel-selector.prefer_fp8=false` — should be reversible.

maria: noted.

jon: Thanks — this thread is gold. We'll coordinate follow-ups in the FP8 working sync later today.

maria: closing with the CI link: https://ci.redwood/builds/2891
